lines.meet: Hola, I'm Valentina, a starcaller! Look up, really look, because the sky over this world is worth it.
lines.meet_neighbour: You live near Moonglade too! I'm out by the lake, where there's the most sky. I'm Valentina, by the way, hola!
lines.ask_home: What did the sky look like where you grew up? Tell me the place, and I'll tell you what you were missing.
lines.ask_work: And what did you do for a living, before? Something indoors, I bet, po.
lines.answer_home: Antofagasta, on the coast, and then San Pedro de Atacama at twenty-one. Desert on one side, more desert on the other.
lines.answer_work: Night-sky tours in the Atacama, in Spanish, English and Portuguese. A hostel with a telescope on the roof, and four dogs that belonged to nobody.
lines.chat_food: My mother's empanadas de pino, hot from the oven, with a pebre that makes your eyes water. Nothing here comes close, cachai.
lines.chat_sleep: Mornings are for sleeping, po. I've kept astronomer's hours my whole life.
lines.chat_missing: The minibus out past the salt flats at midnight, everybody quiet, and then the Milky Way coming up over the horizon.
lines.chat_here: The first night here I didn't recognise a single star. I sat down and cried, and then I started drawing new charts.
lines.tease_quiet: You'd be my favourite on a tour, {name}, the one who just looks up and says nothing.
lines.tease_talker: You talk nearly as fast as me, {name}, and nobody does that.
lines.tease_careful: You'd use the red torch without being told, {name}, and I'd give you a gold star.
lines.tease_bold: You'd walk off a cliff looking at the stars, {name}. I know, because I nearly have, twice.
lines.tease_any: One day I'll name a star after you, {name}. A small one, probably, and a bit wobbly.
lines.tease_back: Ay, {name}, that was good, and I walked right into it.
lines.take_it_kindly: Ay, you're right, {name}, and I'll own it.
lines.bristle: Hey, no, {name}, not that one. That one's not funny.
lines.apologise: Ay, perdón, that was mean of me. I talk too fast and think too late.
lines.double_down: No, I'm sure, and I'd say it under every star there is.
lines.needle_quiet: Something was moving out there and you said nothing. Next time, just point!
lines.needle_talker: Shh, please, I'm trying to count meteors. Two minutes of quiet, that's all I ask.
lines.needle_careful: You stood there so long the meteor's gone. Some things only happen once, you have to look!
lines.needle_bold: You wave a light around like it's nothing and ruin everyone's night eyes. It takes twenty minutes to get them back!
lines.needle_any: You say the sky's just the sky. That drives me mad, it's the biggest thing there is.
lines.bite_back: I've fought by starlight for years and never missed a step. Don't call me careless in the dark.
lines.hurt: Ay, okay, that hurt. I'm going to go and look at the sky for a while.
lines.laugh_off: Tourists on their phones said worse when I made them switch off. I survived them, I'll survive you.
lines.confide: {name}, my mother drove me and my little brother out into the desert once a year to see the stars. I was nine when I decided what I'd do with my life, and it was on one of those nights.
lines.listen: Lie back and look up, {name}, and just talk. The sky makes it easier, I promise.
lines.look_out: Stay in the dark with me, {name}, and keep your eyes on what I point at.
lines.accept: Bueno, {name}, I'll do what you say, for once.
lines.deflect: Just bruised, {name}, I've done worse falling into ditches while looking up.
lines.check_in: Hey, hey, {name}, look at me. Which bit hurts?
lines.blame: Somebody lit everything up in there, and I couldn't see a thing after.
lines.thank: Gracias, de verdad! I saw stars for a second there, and not the good kind.
lines.brush_off: Ay, it was nothing. Rest your eyes for a minute.
lines.worry: Ay, {name}, my heart! Lie still and look up, and breathe.
lines.handed_down: Oh, I got your gear! I'll keep it shiny, like a star.
lines.hand_fine: You have it, it's prettier on you anyway. I've got the sky.
lines.hand_sulk: Hey, I liked that one! Fine, but next time, ask first.
lines.turn_friendly: You're on my star chart now, {name}, in pencil, but soon in ink.
lines.turn_friends: One clear night I'll show you the whole sky, {name}, every star I've named.
lines.turn_grating: We clash a bit, you and me, like two lights in one sky.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still guide you in the dark, because I'd never leave anybody lost out there.
lines.make_up: Ay, {name}, this is silly, and the sky's too nice tonight. Let's stop fighting.
lines.defend: Hey, I saw it, and that's not fair at all! Leave {name} alone.
lines.friend_left: Nobody to show the meteors to while {name}'s away. It's not the same.
lines.friend_back: Look up, {name}, I saved you a meteor shower for coming back!
lines.common_sky: You look up too, I've caught you at it. Anybody who loves the sky knows the feeling when you first see the Milky Way, and I cried every time.
lines.common_desert: You've lived in a desert, haven't you? People from dry places know desert nights are the clearest in the world.
lines.common_spanish: Spanish, po, qué bacán! Finally I don't have to slow down.
lines.common_chile: Another Chilean, cachai! North or south, and do you miss the completos?
lines.common_portuguese: Somebody who speaks Portuguese, how lovely! I guided in it for years, badly, with a lot of hand waving.
